note: Require Revision Log Message makes the node revision log message a required field for selected content types. Its entire persistent state is one config object, require_revision_log_message.adminsettings, with two keys: content_types (a sequence of node-type machine names the rule applies to) and require_for_new_nodes (boolean; when FALSE the rule only fires on edits of existing nodes). Two permissions: administer require_revision_log_message (settings form access) and bypass require_revision_log_message (skip the requirement). Configure route require_revision_log_message.admin_settings_form at /admin/config/require-revision-log/adminsettings. No services, plugins, drush, or entities. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object and verified with drush; the shipped baseline is content_types {} + require_for_new_nodes false (the config object does not exist on a fresh install).

evals.prompt: In the Drupal contrib module require_revision_log_message, which config object and key store the list of content types that must have a revision log message filled in?
evals.expected_output: The config object require_revision_log_message.adminsettings holds a content_types sequence of node-type machine names; a type is 'on' when its machine name is a value in that list. A separate boolean require_for_new_nodes controls whether the rule also applies to new nodes.

evals.prompt: A site admin wants some editors to be exempt from require_revision_log_message so they can save nodes without a revision log message. Which permission do they need, and what is the other permission this module defines?
evals.expected_output: Grant the exempt role the 'bypass require_revision_log_message' permission (the form alter early-returns for users who have it). The other permission, 'administer require_revision_log_message', gates the settings form.

evals.prompt: By default, does require_revision_log_message force a revision log message when an editor creates a brand-new node, or only when editing an existing one? How do you change that?
evals.expected_output: By default it only applies when editing an existing node (a new node is skipped because require_for_new_nodes defaults to FALSE). Enable require_for_new_nodes (tick 'Require revision log message for new nodes' on the settings form) to also enforce it on node creation.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, require_revision_log_message is enabled and configured. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which content type(s) are set to require a revision log message.
evals.expected_output: The content type blog_post requires a revision log message: require_revision_log_message.adminsettings -> content_types contains { blog_post: blog_post }.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is require_revision_log_message currently configured to require a revision log message when creating NEW nodes (not just when editing existing ones)? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: Yes. require_revision_log_message.adminsettings -> require_for_new_nodes is TRUE, so the log message is required on new nodes as well as edits.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the require_revision_log_message module to make the Article content type require a revision log message. Apply the change to the live site's configuration.
evals.expected_output: In require_revision_log_message.adminsettings, content_types includes 'article' (e.g. set content_types to {article: article} via the settings form or config API and save).

evals.prompt: Article already requires a revision log message on this site, but only when editing existing articles. Configure require_revision_log_message so that a revision log message is also required when creating a brand-new node. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: Set require_revision_log_message.adminsettings -> require_for_new_nodes to TRUE (tick 'Require revision log message for new nodes' on the settings form, or set it via the config API and save).
